subject: Halcyon: request for tenant-level token cap + per-request circuit breaker (close timeline)
messages:

Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@halcyonfin.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Halcyon: token cap ask and per-request circuit breaker (timeline)

Marissa / Priyom —

Quick background: Halcyon is finalizing legal and procurement but procurement has a hard requirement we didn’t anticipate: they need a tenant-level monthly token cap that we can enforce server-side (not just billing alerts) plus a per-request circuit breaker that will reject calls once a tenant's monthly cap is reached. This is a gating item for their security team and procurement — they will not sign without it.

They described the ask like this in procurement: "We require a hard enforcement mechanism that prevents runaway token usage per tenant and an integration point for us to receive pre-authorization denials for requests that would exceed the cap." They also want an audit trail showing when the cap hit and which API keys were blocked.

From our side the deal economics and discount we offered assume we can close by 2027-05-15. If we push the timeline we risk the exec sponsor going quiet and they’ll ask for a deeper discount.

Can Product/Eng provide:
- Feasibility assessment by EOD Mon (Apr 5)
- Proposed implementation: short design + security considerations
- ETA for an EAP (preview) we could offer (we'd accept a 'preview feature' note in contract)

Attachments: Halcyon MUP (mutual action plan) + procurement note.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Halcyon: token cap ask and per-request circuit breaker (timeline)

Ben — thanks for summarizing. Copying initial thoughts so we have a record before I loop Eng: 

Short answer: technically feasible with two pieces: (1) server-side quota enforcement per-tenant + rate-limit windowing; (2) a lightweight preflight API that can be called to validate/authorize a request against the tenant quota before executing generation. Audit trail can be recorded via existing request logs + a small event when the quota transitions to "exhausted."

Security implications: will need KMS-backed tenant identifier mapping, and the enforcement path must be in the high-performance ingress to avoid adding latency to normal requests. We'll need to validate that the enforcement path plays nicely with batching and KV cache (we should not evict cache entries on quota checks).

Workaround (short-term): we could offer a billing-only cap and immediate webhook notifications when usage exceeds thresholds so Halcyon can opt to block on their side; not ideal for procurement but buys time.

I will get Eng to scope an EAP design doc and flag if this touches core runtime batching plumbing. Priyom
Staff Solutions Engineer

Ben / Priyom / Aisha —

Thanks for the heads up, Ben. Halcyon's requirement is reasonable for regulated customers but this will require a small cross-team effort. Priyom has captured the components. From Product perspective here's how we can proceed: 

1) Priority: I'll mark this PRIO-7423 as "deal-driven" and propose we allocate a smallship sprint (2 engineers, 3 weeks) to deliver an EAP focused on enforcement + audit events (no UI in phase 1).

2) Scope for EAP:
   - tenant-level monthly cap enforcement (configurable via API/console for admin API keys)
   - preflight/authorize endpoint that returns OK/Rejected with reason codes
   - audit events written to existing event stream and a new "quota_transition" field in request logs
   - docs + config guide for Halcyon procurement and security team

3) Non-goal for EAP: full console UI, multi-tenant throttling policies, or per-user caps. Those can be follow-ups.

Constraints: We cannot introduce per-request high-latency checks into the hot path. Engineering will need to confirm whether the preflight can be implemented as a fast in-memory check or requires a persist call that would increase P95. Priyom, can you capture a microbenchmark and propose the fast-path?

We can offer Halcyon an "EAP access" clause in the MUP: they accept preview disclaimers and we provide the capability with standard SLAs for preview. If Halcyon accepts, Legal can draft a narrow amendment.

Aisha — would Halcyon accept an EAP (preview) for contract purposes if we commit to delivery by 2027-05-15 and provide an audit log export as part of the preview? If not, please let us know the non-negotiable requirements so we can re-evaluate.

Marissa

Marissa / Ben / Priyom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed plan. Halcyon's security and procurement teams discussed and are willing to accept an EAP/preview for the enforcement feature provided the following are met in writing: 

- Delivery commitment: preview usable in production by 2027-05-15 for our tenant only.
- Auditability: logs with timestamped "quota_transition" events and the API key/tenant id that triggered it.
- Fail-safe: when the cap is hit, requests must be rejected with a standard error code we can program against (429 or 470; Halcyon will prefer 470 to differentiate).
- Data residency note: audit events must be retained for 12 months and be exportable to their S3 bucket (they will supply S3 details; they will sign an addendum).

If Redwood can confirm these three items in an amendment to the MUP we will proceed to signature and agree to the discount discussed. Procurement prefers the amendment text rather than product-only promises.

Next steps from our side: procurement will send a short amendment template to Legal once you confirm the delivery commitment.

Aisha Khan
VP, Technology Operations
Halcyon Financial
